title: Safety window refactor: quick notes & test ideas
content:
Notes to self / review dump for the "safety window" refactor (PR #2142) - rough, noisy, intentionally shallow in places.

Context:
- Purpose: reduce KV-prefix cache churn for high-request-churn workloads by introducing a 'safety window' that keeps short-lived prefixes pinned for a configurable TTL before eviction. Goal: reduce token-generation latency spikes under bursty traffic.
- Approach: when a request touches a prefix, mark it 'in-safety' and delay eviction for TTL_SAFETY secs. Evictions still happen if memory pressure is high. New opt-in config: SAFETY_WINDOW_ENABLE + TTL_SAFETY_MS.
- Scope in this PR: core algorithm + unit tests + a tiny metrics hook. Not included: rollout toggle wiring, infra defaults, or dashboard panels.

High-level concerns to call out in PR description:
- Backwards compatibility: default should be OFF. If turned ON, memory footprint increases briefly — need ops signoff.
- Observability: added metric safety_window_pinned_count and safety_window_evictions_skipped; must chart before rollout.
- Failure modes: if TTL too long, cache becomes sticky -> OOM. If TTL too short, no benefit.

Quick checklist (what I want reviewers to focus on)
- [ ] Correctness of eviction guard: make sure we still respect hard memory thresholds even for pinned items. (see eviction_manager.go: lines ~130-165)
- [ ] Race conditions around marking prefix in-safety while concurrent requests mutate KV cache. Critical section should be under cache.mu but double-check lock ordering with coordinator.mu.
- [ ] Metrics labeling: ensure pinned_count is tagged by model and region. Avoid high-cardinality tags (do not include request_id).
- [ ] Tests: unit test for TTL expiration + simulated memory-pressure forced-eviction. Integration test sketch below.
- [ ] Performance: microbenchmark on small gpu instance with seq-len distribution similar to prod (p95 ~ 120 tokens).

Tests to add (prioritized)
1) Unit: pin/unpin lifecycle (fast, deterministic)
   - create cache, set TTL_SAFETY=50ms, touch key, assert pinned==1, wait 60ms, assert pinned==0
   - forced evict: simulate memory pressure and confirm pinned items are evicted when threshold_exceeded==true
2) Concurrency test:
   - 100 goroutines touching same prefix while evict loop runs; assert no panic, and reference counts remain sane
3) Integration (dockerized scenario):
   - small harness that sends bursts (100 rps pulses, 5s on / 10s off) for 2 minutes; measure 95th latency with safety enabled vs disabled
   - assert end-to-end latency regression < 10% and dropped evictions > 30% (rough target)
4) Regression: ensure dedup cache behavior unchanged (dedup currently relies on immediate evict semantics)

Risk mitigations / rollout plan (ops friendly)
- Step 0: keep default OFF and ship behind feature flag; add feature in remote config store
- Step 1: dogfood in staging with synthetic load (use staging-k8s single-gpu), enable for non-critical models only
- Step 2: enable in dedicated for small customer segment with extra telemetry retention
- If latency or memory problems -> reduce TTL to 200ms, or disable entirely.

Metrics to watch during rollout
- safety_window_pinned_count (gauge)
- safety_window_evictions_skipped_total (counter)
- memory_resident_bytes (gauge)
- token_gen_p95_latency_ms (per-model)

Code spots to review carefully
- eviction_manager.go: new function tryPinPrefix() - I'm slightly worried about the early return when found=false (line ~78). Could skip intended side-effects.
- cache/kv.go: AddPinnedState uses a pointer on an object pooled by sync.Pool. Confirm we don't retain pooled object in a global map (could cause reuse-after-free).
- coordinator/request_router.go: I introduced a short-circuit to avoid pinning for requests flagged as 'ephemeral'. Is the ephemeral flag always set by upper layers? Potential NPE if header missing.

Small local debug script I used: (handy for reviewers to reproduce)
- scripts/run_safety_sim.sh: spins a small harness; args: --ttl-ms 500 --burst 200 --duration 60. Output: CSV of latency, pinned_count.

Open questions (ask in review thread)
- Is the TTL unit ms or seconds? I used ms to allow fine control, but ops prefers seconds in remote config. Should we convert?
- Should we surface an eviction reason enum that includes 'pinned_evicted' vs 'normal_evicted'? Helps dashboards but complicates eviction hot-path.
- Are there performance expectations on GC pressure from additional structs? We added ~24 bytes per pinned entry. Is that acceptable?

Follow-ups (post-merge issues)
- add dashboard panels and an alert when safety_window_pinned_count > X for > 5m (post-merge INF ticket)
- wire feature flag for infra team to control per-customer rollout
- explore adaptive TTL: start short, extend if reuse pattern detected
- run longer soak (24h) on staging with heavy multi-tenant mix

Suggested reviewers: Aisha (locking/race), Diego (eviction semantics), Kai (perf microbench), Samir (SRE/alerts)

Notes to self before merging:
- make sure CHANGELOG entry is brief and includes default OFF + ops note
- add example env var lines to README/config docs
- bump metric names in observability infra repo (open PR there first)

Random scribbles:
- Consider TTL jitter to avoid synchronized expiration waves - add +-10% jitter on TTL expiry
- Might be able to implement pin as just an incremented refcount combined with expiration queue - avoids separate pinned map
- If we see too much memory, consider LRU-with-pinned-escape (pinned items are moved to separate list with capacity limit)

End of dump. Will tidy for actual PR description later. If anything here is unclear, ping me in #dev-rare or add comments directly to PR.

-- Ben
